title: Beyond Text: Probing K-12 Educators’ Perspectives on Designing Learning Opportunities Leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models
extended_summary:
This paper examines how K-12 educators envision using multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for learning, and what concerns arise when teachers try to design educational experiences with them. The authors focus on a gap in the literature: while many AI-for-education papers discuss student-facing applications or teacher productivity tools, less is known about what educators themselves think about emerging multimodal AI capabilities beyond text.

To investigate this, the researchers ran workshops with 12 K-12 educators in New York City. Participants viewed demo videos of commercial MLLMs, discussed possible classroom uses, and then prototyped their own learning activities using Claude 3.5 and its Artifacts feature. The sample included public school, charter school, magnet school, and museum educators teaching elementary, middle, and high school students, with varied years of experience and mostly novice familiarity with LLMs. The workshop format let participants experiment with image input, text prompting, and interactive code-based outputs.

The paper finds that educators were broadly enthusiastic about MLLMs, especially for creating multimedia simulations, personalized supports, research scaffolds, and interactive learning tools. However, many teachers preferred using MLLMs themselves to generate student-facing materials rather than having students interact directly with the model, especially in elementary and middle grades. High school educators were more open to student-direct use. The authors conclude that MLLMs may be useful for teacher-authored interactive content and student research support, but they also highlight concerns about output quality, literacy-level fit, access, policy, and the need for professional development.

identified_tools.name: Claude
identified_tools.description: Anthropic’s conversational large language model assistant capable of text and image input, with code-based interactive output via Artifacts.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in a November 2024 workshop with 12 K-12 educators to prototype student-facing learning activities, test multimodal inputs/outputs, and explore educator perspectives on designing with multimodal LLMs.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative workshop study with 12 educators using a commercial AI tool, not an experimental impact study. It provides rich descriptive evidence about educator perceptions and design choices, but no causal estimate of learning effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports no measured student outcomes or effect sizes. Its contribution is mainly prospective and design-oriented, so the educational impact is suggested rather than demonstrated.
